title: Renewal & expansion check-in - Orion Retail
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on capacity upgrades, adding EU region, and potential 12-month contract extension for discounted reserved capacity. Customer needs predictable latency during peak sales windows and audit-ready security docs. Redwood to send updated pricing and run a quick benchmark for Orion's multi-region config.
action_items: Sofia Patel: Send updated pricing sheet with 1yr/2yr reserved options and regional rates - due 2026-04-14
Dan Liu: Run 2-region (NA+EU) benchmark with Orion sample workload and share results + latency percentiles - due 2026-04-17
Carlos Ruiz (Orion): Share current token volumes, peak QPS, and expected growth for next 12 months - due 2026-04-13
Sofia Patel: Share SOC2 summary and relevant security docs link - due 2026-04-12
next_steps: Redwood to provide updated pricing + reserved capacity options
SE to run quick latency/cost benchmark for NA+EU setup
Customer to review security docs and confirm procurement timeline
Schedule follow-up call week of 2026-04-20 to review benchmarks and finalize term
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Dan Liu (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Orion Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Orion Infra Lead), Priya Kapoor (Orion Procurement)

---
00:00 Sofia Patel: hey everyone, thanks for making time today. quick check-in — how's the run rate looking this quarter?
00:15 Maya Singh: yeah thanks so much. overall things have been good, traffic spiked during the spring promo and we hit some higher latencies in EU, which is what we wanted to talk about, we are thinking more about adding EU region and also locking a longer term commit.
00:34 Carlos Ruiz: hi all, and just to add, during peak we saw tail latency out to 600-700 ms on a few p99 checks, so exploring dedicated capacity or region-specific routing would help. also curious about costs if we go reserved.
00:50 Dan Liu: got it. yeah that tail makes sense, likely due to cold-starts across regions and the current cross-region routing. we can do autoscale + dedicated pools per region or a shared dedicated with routing rules. tradeoffs there.
01:10 Priya Kapoor: quick one from procurement side — if we extend to a 12‑month term with reserved capacity, what kind of discounts are typical? also need timeline for legal review.
01:25 Sofia Patel: great q. typical discounts for 12 month reserved are 12-18% depending on committed GPU*hours and region mix, 24 months ~ 20-25%. i will send an updated pricing sheet after the call.
01:38 Maya Singh: when you say committed GPU hours — is that per region or pooled?
01:45 Dan Liu: currently Redwood supports both models. you can reserve per-region dedicated pools or reserve a global pool and pin region routing. pooling gives flexibility but per-region can reduce cross-region latency. sometimes we recommend a small committed per-region + burst capacity.
02:10 Carlos Ruiz: that makes sense. for us EU is new so we'd probably want a modest pool there to start. what are onboarding steps for a new region — any infra changes on our side?
02:23 Dan Liu: for Redwood Private (VPC) we need a connector peered into the EU region; for Hosted/Dedicated we can spin it up from our side and provide endpoint + routing. that said, for data residency we can enable EU-only processing if needed. note — in some transcripts i see V-P-C written as VPC, but just to be clear, we do region peering.
02:45 Carlos Ruiz: right, we'll want EU-only processing for certain datasets. we'll need KMS integration details for key management as well.
02:52 Sofia Patel: noted, i'll include KMS/HSM integration notes and SOC2 docs.
03:00 Maya Singh: on the performance side, can you run a benchmark using our prompt mix? we have a bunch of short convo prompts and some long generation prompts.
03:12 Dan Liu: yes we can. if you can share a sample payload distribution (token length histogram + qps patterns) we'll run a NA+EU 2-region bench and return p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens estimate.
03:28 Maya Singh: i'll share that after the call.
03:32 Priya Kapoor: timeline — we have an internal renewal decision meeting on 2026-04-23, procurement needs finalized terms one week prior. is that feasible?
03:42 Sofia Patel: yes, that's doable. if we run the benchmark this week and share pricing by 4/14 we should have time to iterate before your 4/23 decision.
03:50 Carlos Ruiz: any gotchas on model compatibility? we're running a mix of open models and a few private tuned variants.
03:58 Dan Liu: we support most open models and custom variants, but for private tuned models we recommend pinned versions on dedicated pools to keep KV cache warm and avoid cross-variant eviction. sometimes latency spikes are due to quantization mismatches or kernel fallbacks; we'll surface those in the bench.
04:20 Maya Singh: are there any integrations with our monitoring stack — we run Datadog and Splunk.
04:26 Sofia Patel: yes, Redwood Console supports Datadog metrics and can push traces; Splunk can ingest audit logs. i'll share the docs link in the follow-up.
04:36 Priya Kapoor: security: we need audit logs for compliance and SOC2 paper. also SAML/SSO for users.
04:44 Sofia Patel: we have SSO/SAML and RBAC, plus audit logs available; SOC2 report available on request. i'll attach the security packet.
04:55 Carlos Ruiz: quick question — competitor eval popped up: some teams are testing Bedrock and Anthropic. how does Redwood differ on cost predictability?
05:06 Sofia Patel: good point. our focus is on inference economics — tooling to control batching, kv cache, and route policies to reduce unit cost. that'll show in the benchmark where we'll compare baseline hosted vs dedicated reserved.
05:20 Dan Liu: also we provide per-token cost breakouts in Console so you can see what's driving the bill.
05:28 Maya Singh: okay, sounds good. can you outline recommended config for a 2-region (NA primary, EU secondary) setup for our traffic shape?
05:38 Dan Liu: recommended starting config: small dedicated pool in EU (2 GPUs), medium pool in NA (4 GPUs), routing policy: geo-aware with fallback to NA for non-EU residency traffic; autoscale thresholds tuned for promo peaks. we'll validate these numbers with your traffic sample.
06:00 Carlos Ruiz: what's the expected hit to latency if we route cross-region for cold KV hits?
06:07 Dan Liu: cross-region cold KV can add 80-150 ms, depending on sequence length and backend. with prefix caching and pinned variants that usually goes down to ~20-50 ms. we'll quantify in the bench. note transcription noise: sometimes systems say "K-V cash" in auto transcribe.
06:30 Priya Kapoor: on contract terms — if we take 12 months with reserve, do we get dedicated support or SLA changes?
06:37 Sofia Patel: reserved contracts include a support tier; enterprise plans have SLA-backed latency targets and priority escalation. i'll include the SLA summary in the package.
06:46 Maya Singh: small point — our legal wants to see data deletion/retention policy.
06:50 Sofia Patel: yes, data retention controls are configurable; we'll attach the policy doc.
06:56 Carlos Ruiz: ok thanks. one more ops thing — if we add EU, will billing be consolidated or per-region?
07:02 Sofia Patel: billing can be consolidated under one invoice, with line items per region. we can also create separate billing entities if needed.
07:10 Maya Singh: great. any estimated timeline for spinning up EU region on Dedicated?
07:14 Dan Liu: if it's hosted/dedicated from Redwood side we can spin within 5-10 business days after contractual greenlight; VPC/private requires peering and could be 2-4 weeks.
07:27 Priya Kapoor: procurement note — i'll need final contract terms by 4/15 to hit our internal deadlines.
07:33 Sofia Patel: understood, we'll target delivering the pricing and docs by 4/14.
07:37 ---
27:00 [mid-call technical deep dive / bench scope chat summarized]
27:10 Dan Liu: for the bench i'll run a continuous arrival pattern with burst windows to emulate promo traffic, include KV cache warm and cold runs, and capture per-model kernel fallback logs. i'll also share a small spreadsheet with assumptions.
27:30 Maya Singh: that helps, thanks.
27:40 Carlos Ruiz: we'll add the token distribution and expected growth in the sheet.
27:46 Sofia Patel: ok, recapping next steps...
27:52 Sofia Patel: Redwood: send pricing + security docs (SOC2, KMS integration, SLA summary), SE to run NA+EU bench and share results, Orion to share token volumes and timeline. follow up meet week of 4/20.
28:10 Priya Kapoor: sounds good — i'll also start internal paperwork.
28:16 Maya Singh: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.
28:20 Sofia Patel: thank you, we'll be in touch.

---
References shared in call: renewal pricing draft (link: https://redwood.app/s/renewal-deck), bench assumptions spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/s/bench-orion), SOC2 summary (link: https://redwood.app/s/security-packet)

End of transcript.
crm_notes: Customer wants EU region + reserved capacity. Decision timeline 2026-04-23. Procurement needs final terms one week prior.
notes: Transcript contains minor auto-transcription artifacts (e.g., 'K-V cash' for KV cache, 'V-P-C' for VPC). AE+SE present. Call ends with clear next steps and timeline.
